title: Niraparib (Zejula) tablets
context_label: Maintenance after a response to platinum chemotherapy
schedule_label: Take the prescribed dose once every day. A 28-day cycle is a way of recording treatment. There is no planned tablet-free week.
schedule_summary: Take the prescribed dose once every day. A 28-day cycle is a way of recording treatment. There is no planned tablet-free week.
purpose: These tablets help delay the return or growth of ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer after it has responded to platinum chemotherapy.
indication_text: Your team will explain whether this is maintenance after first treatment for advanced disease or after platinum-sensitive relapse.
administration_text: Swallow the tablets whole with water at the same time each day, either with a light meal or at least one hour before or two hours after food. If you miss a dose or vomit after it, take the next scheduled dose. Do not take an extra tablet.
monitoring_summary: The NCCP lists blood pressure at week 2, monthly for 6 months and then every 3 months. The European product information calls for at least weekly readings for the first 2 months, monthly during the first year and periodically thereafter. Agree a written monitoring plan with your team before starting.
review_status: Feasibility build; independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending

agents.name: Niraparib
agents.explanation: Niraparib blocks proteins that help repair damaged DNA. This can slow the growth of some cancer cells.
agents.mechanism: Niraparib blocks proteins that help repair damaged DNA. This can slow the growth of some cancer cells.
agents.watch: Report unusual bruising, bleeding, fever, headaches or racing heartbeat.

common_effects.title: Nausea and constipation
common_effects.text: Ask for an anti-sickness plan before starting. Let the team know early if constipation is affecting eating or drinking.

common_effects.title: Tiredness
common_effects.text: Keep track of changes in what you can manage. A blood test can help identify anaemia.

serious_effects.title: Low blood counts
serious_effects.text: Unusual bleeding, infection or new breathlessness needs urgent assessment. Persistent abnormalities may need assessment for rare bone marrow disorders including MDS or AML.

serious_effects.title: High blood pressure
serious_effects.text: Report severe headache, confusion or changes in vision urgently. Call 112 or 999 for a seizure, collapse, chest pain or severe breathing difficulty.

phases.label: Daily treatment at home
phases.detail: Swallow the tablets whole with water at the same time each day, either with a light meal or at least one hour before or two hours after food. If you miss a dose or vomit after it, take the next scheduled dose. Do not take an extra tablet.

anatomy: Get urgent help for sudden severe headache, confusion or visual change. A seizure needs 112 or 999.
Check as advised. Report palpitations, headache or unusually high readings.
Call for new breathlessness, dizziness or marked tiredness.
Use your prescribed anti-sickness medicine. Call if you cannot keep fluids down.
Call promptly for new bruises, nosebleeds, bleeding gums or blood in urine or stool.
Call immediately for fever, shaking chills or sudden illness, even with a normal temperature.
anatomy_note: Call for new or worsening symptoms.

questions.q: Can you show when your next blood count and blood pressure check are due, and explain what to do after a missed tablet?
questions.a: Review your personal plan with the team before leaving.

questions.q: Who do I call outside clinic hours?
questions.a: Ask the team to complete both numbers on the wallet card and agree a backup contact.

support.title: At home
support.text: Follow your prescribed anti-sickness plan. Bedtime dosing may help nausea. Speak to the team before changing the dose or stopping.

support.title: Other medicines
support.text: Show your team all medicines, including blood thinners, aspirin and supplements. Do not stop prescribed medicines on your own.

support.title: Family planning
support.text: Niraparib can harm a developing baby. Discuss contraception, fertility and breastfeeding before starting.

teachback: Can you show when your next blood count and blood pressure check are due, and explain what to do after a missed tablet?
consent_support: Discuss the expected benefit, side effects, fertility, alternatives and symptom-directed care with the treating clinician. You may ask for more time or change your decision.
safety_note: Fever, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness or a severe headache? Call oncology now.

evidence.title: Evidence behind this treatment
evidence.interpretation: PRIMA studied first-line maintenance after platinum response. The risk of progression or death was lower with niraparib than placebo in the homologous-recombination-deficient group (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31–0.59). NOVA separately studied maintenance after platinum-sensitive relapse.
evidence.limitations: The first-line and relapse studies enrolled different populations. Delayed progression is a group result and does not establish a survival benefit for an individual.

monitoring_schedule.title: Checks and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Weight, blood count, blood pressure, kidney and liver tests
Weight and platelets help the team select your starting dose.

rows.label: First month
cells: Blood count weekly. Check blood pressure with the team.
Have the next test dates written down before starting.

rows.label: Ongoing
cells: Blood count monthly for the next 10 months, then periodically. Kidney and liver tests monthly.
Continue blood pressure checks. Your team may ask for more frequent home readings.

sections.title: Prescription and supply
sections.text: Check tablet strength and dose on the latest label. Arrange repeat supplies before running out. Ask what to do if the team pauses treatment.

sections.title: Home monitoring
sections.text: Bring your blood pressure readings, tablet list, symptoms and dates of any missed doses to each review.

continuous_oral.title: The first two weeks
continuous_oral.text: Ask whether to take an anti-sickness medicine during the first two weeks and which medicine to use if you feel sick despite it. Your team will write down the medicine, dose and timing.
